---
title: "Course Starter and Workflows"
---

Use **Codex first**, or **Claude as a supported alternative**. Both follow the same local written procedures. These are plain-text prompts, not installed slash commands. You do not need the original course's external template or Claude-only skills.

## Course starter {#course-starter}

1. [Download the course starter](course-support/byui-product-management-starter.zip) and extract it into a new folder for your own project, outside cloud-synced folders.
2. Open that folder in VS Code or your agent's desktop workspace. Keep it separate from the shared course website repository.
3. Start `codex` in its terminal, or `claude` if you selected the alternative. Finish [Computer Setup](00-computer-setup.qmd) first if needed.
4. Paste the setup prompt below. It checks what is done and can resume when you reopen the project.

The starter includes `course-schedule.json` with the current dates and first-class exception. It also contains `AGENTS.md` for Codex, `CLAUDE.md` for the Claude alternative, a README context declaration, sprint templates, shared `course-prompts/`, and folders for sprint work, learning, discovery, design, product, specs, go-to-market, metrics, and decisions. Templates are starting points; your actual answers and finished work are the deliverables.

Course LMS and link: ________. Course communication channel: ________. Professor GitHub username: ________. TA GitHub username: ________. Use the [assignment checklist](00-assignments.qmd) for the published sprint dates and proposed exam windows. Leave staff details blank until supplied; the agent must not run commands with placeholder values.

## Setup prompt {#setup-prompt}

Paste this into Codex or Claude inside your extracted starter folder:

```text
Read AGENTS.md, README.md, and course-prompts/setup.md in this folder.
Guide me through the setup procedure one question at a time. Check what is
already done before making changes. Use my own answers for my role and plan.
Read course-schedule.json for deadlines; do not guess staff usernames. Never ask for passwords or tokens.
```

[Read the full setup procedure](course-support/starter/course-prompts/setup.md).

## Sprint plan {#sprint-plan}

Write the plan by the Saturday before Sprints 2–6 begin, or return when your plan changes. Write Sprint 1's plan during the first class. All six wrap-ups are due Saturdays, February 27 through April 3:

```text
Read AGENTS.md, README.md, and course-prompts/sprint-plan.md.
Help me plan my current sprint one question at a time. Ask which sprint
and use my answers for Goal, Why this, Done looks like, and Predicted difficulty.
If a plan exists, preserve it and record what changed and why.
```

[Read the full planning procedure](course-support/starter/course-prompts/sprint-plan.md). The plan lives at `sprints/sprint-N-plan.md`; submit its GitHub link through the course LMS. See the [assignment checklist](00-assignments.qmd) for the exact Saturday deadline or the first-class Sprint 1 exception.

## Sprint review {#sprint-review}

At the end of the sprint:

```text
Read AGENTS.md, README.md, and course-prompts/sprint-review.md.
Help me review my current sprint. Confirm the sprint window and the projects
and evidence I authorize you to read. Show me the work report, then ask the
five retrospective questions one at a time. Preserve my answers word for word.
Mark missing evidence unknown. Let me review the files before submission.
```

[Read the full review procedure](course-support/starter/course-prompts/sprint-review.md). The review lives at `sprints/sprint-N-review.md`. Submit its GitHub link and your Loom demo link. See the [assignment checklist](00-assignments.qmd) for the exact Saturday deadline or the first-class Sprint 1 exception. The [Assessments page](00-assessments.qmd#sprints) defines the deliverables and grading.

## Learn a section {#learn}

Use **Learn with Codex** or the **Claude** alternative beside a chapter heading. Each copies a prompt for that exact section on the current course site. You can also paste:

```text
Read course-prompts/learn.md and tutor me on this course section: <paste URL>.
Ask one question at a time and wait for my answers. If you cannot access the
section, ask me to paste its text. Ask before saving a short learning log.
```

[Read the full tutoring procedure](course-support/starter/course-prompts/learn.md). If you have not downloaded the starter, the copied chapter prompt also includes a self-contained tutoring procedure, so it works in either agent without installing anything.
